title: JevCoder: When Does Decision Delegation Pay Off in Code Repair?
abstract: arXiv:2610.19596v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A coding agent repeatedly makes decisions as it repairs code. These decisions shape repair trajectories and affect the token cost of successive model requests. We ask which repair decisions can be delegated to a low-cost probabilistic judge to reduce token use while maintaining repair quality. The judges answer questions with probabilities over predefined answers, without generating explanations. We evaluate judgment quality across repair stages and test how individual interventions change subsequent repair work. We compare these interventions with unguided repair, which uses no judge, and with the same workflow using the repair model itself as the judge. The benefit depends on the work an intervention changes, rather than the cost of the judgment alone. Based on these studies, we propose JevCoder, a workflow built around Jev, a low-cost probabilistic judge. It combines code-snippet recommendations with action-type guidance and uses judg

translated_title: JevCoder：决策委托何时能在代码修复中带来收益？
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.19596v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：代码修复智能体在修复代码的过程中需要反复做出各种决策。这些决策塑造了修复轨迹，并影响后续模型请求的 token 成本。我们探讨哪些修复决策可以委托给一个低成本的概率判断器，以便在保持修复质量的同时减少 token 使用量。该判断器通过在预定义答案上输出概率来回答问题，而不生成任何解释。我们评估了判断质量在修复各阶段的表现，并测试单项干预如何改变后续的修复工作。我们将这些干预与不使用判断器的无引导修复进行对比，也与使用修复模型自身作为判断器的相同工作流程进行对比。研究表明，干预的收益取决于它所改变的修复工作量，而不仅仅是判断本身的成本。基于这些研究，我们提出了 JevCoder，一个围绕低成本概率判断器 Jev 构建的工作流程。它将代码片段推荐与动作类型指导相结合，并使用判断（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出 JevCoder，一个围绕低成本概率判断器 Jev 构建的代码修复工作流程，系统研究了哪些修复决策可以委托给低成本判断器，通过结合代码片段推荐与动作类型指导，在保持修复质量的同时降低 token 开销。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes JevCoder, a code repair workflow built around a low-cost probabilistic judge called Jev, which systematically studies which repair decisions can be delegated to a cheap judge and combines code-snippet recommendations with action-type guidance to reduce token costs while maintaining repair quality.
